title: A counterexample to Nagamochi's scoring lemma and a new rectangle packing bound
summary: Let $s(N)$ denote the smallest side length of a square containing $N$ unit squares with arbitrary orientations and pairwise disjoint interiors. Nagamochi's Packing Unit Squares in a Rectangle (2005) states a rectangle packing bound from which he deduces two infinite families of exact values: $s(k^2-1) = k$ and $s(k^2-2) = k$ for every integer $k \geq 2$. We construct a family of counterexamples, local to a corner of the container, to the scoring assertion in Nagamochi's Lemma 1.
